title: Temporal & Sequential Words - Time & Order
description: Organize actions in time: pendant (during), avant (before), après (after), d'abord (first), ensuite (then), finalement (finally)
can_do: Sequence events in time (first, then, finally)
Describe when things happen (before, during, after)
Tell stories with proper temporal flow

vocabulary.note: sequence - après le dîner; can be connector or preposition
duration from past - depuis trois ans

concepts.definition: Words that show when or for how long something happens - used with nouns
concepts.example: {pendant des heures} (for hours), {avant le cours} (before class), {après le travail} (after work), {une fois} (once), {cette année} (this year), {en ce moment} (right now); {Après le travail, je bois un café} (After work, I have a coffee)

concepts.definition: Words that show the order of actions - connect sentences smoothly
concepts.example: {D'abord}, {je mange. Ensuite}, {je pars. Finalement}, {j'arrive.} (First, I eat. Then, I leave. Finally, I arrive.)

concepts.definition: Use these words to tell stories and describe routines naturally
concepts.example: Before: '{Je mange. Je pars.}' (choppy) After: '{D'abord, je mange. Ensuite, je pars.}' (smooth!)

concepts.definition: Sequential connectors usually start sentences. Prepositions go before nouns.
concepts.example: {D'abord}, {je pars} (First, I leave). {Je pars après le cours} (I leave after class).

mistakes.feedback: Use '{pendant}' for duration, 'pour' is for purpose/recipient

items.hint: depuis - duration from a point in the past

items.situation: Say 'first' or 'first of all' (to start a sequence)

items.hint: Continues a sequence - most common word

mistakes.feedback: That also works, but '{ensuite}' is more common
That also means 'finally', but '{finalement}' is more common

items.hint: Après + le cours + comma + je révise

items.situation: Say 'For an hour' or 'During an hour'
